decided_by: approved with 3 advisory objection(s) — none high-severity

objections.problem: jsonb_set targets agent_definitions WHERE type='page-build-handler' without filtering is_active/version explicitly in the UPDATE itself; the plan relies on a point-in-time census (1/1/1 active rows) rather than a row-scoped predicate, so a race with another session creating a second active row between measurement and apply is unguarded (this is exactly the class of hazard the 'four agent types have two active rows' landmine describes, even though these three types were measured clean).
Same type-scoped UPDATE pattern as edit 7, same mitigation (1/1/1 census) and same residual staleness risk between measurement and apply.

reviews.notes: This is a thorough resubmission: each of the 8 numbered objections from the gating review is answered by either a real code edit (absent-facts detection edit 3, recompose detection edit 4, lossy-merge durability edit 5), a corrected seed sketch (edit 8's full nested path), a corrected rationale (edit 7's 'two agents, neither wired' retraction), or a discharged precondition (compliance read, DO/RAISE ordering guards). Edits change real things (new functions, new persisted error codes, corrected jsonb paths, ordering guards) — none are audit-only. Causal targeting looks sound: each new edit maps to the specific mechanism the diagnosis named, and known limitations (absent_from_plan can't distinguish drop-vs-rename, FACT_ASSIGNMENT_ABSENT only covers the carry path, PLAN_PAGE_MERGE_LOSSY untested live) are stated rather than hidden. Scope is large but each piece traces to an owner ruling or an upheld objection, and seed 333/features_open/012 are explicitly excluded rather than smuggled in. The two low objections are about the type-scoped UPDATE pattern that the landmine index flags generally; the census evidence mitigates but does not eliminate the risk, hence checks rather than a blocking objection.

objections.problem: recompose_pages escape is enforced only via prose ('only when the briefing explicitly asks...') with no field-level enforcement point — the plan's own risk section admits 'prose is a weaker control than a field.' This is the exact recurring shape 016b §9 already names: 'A recorded user decision with no enforcement point is decorative — an LLM re-guesses it every run.' If the LLM ignores the prose escape, a page's realised composition (and its fact-carried content) is silently recomposed/dropped with only a best-effort observability row (RECOMPOSE_INTENT_NOT_REALISED, itself unable to distinguish drop from rename) after the fact — detection, not prevention.

carrySectionFactsOntoRealised's correctness depends on object-form entries never escaping the 176-line window between reconcilePlanWithRealised (:3101) and the normalise pass (:3277) in ValidateSitePlanAction. This is a structural invariant enforced only by an end-to-end test, not by any type/shape guard in the code itself — a future refactor that reorders or early-returns between those two points silently ships mixed-shape data (object vs string) into pages.sections, whose 15+ readers expect strings. The plan itself flags this as the thing 'a reviewer should check first,' which is itself a signal this is a known-shape latent landmine class (cf. 'A step whose output_field... REPLACES it' and multiple 'shared mechanism, one guarded call site' precedents in the index).

missing: Whether features_open/012 (the deferred permanent field-based fix for recompose_pages enforcement) has any target date or is at risk of indefinite deferral, given the content-loss potential this round explicitly flags but does not close.
reviews.notes: Architecture-level flag for a human: this plan is one of several in this lane (bugs_open/087, 214, 215, features_open/012) that repeatedly hits the same shape — a plan-time decision (recompose eligibility, richer-wins merge, fact assignment) enforced through an LLM prompt or best-effort log rather than a schema/field the render path must honor. The plan's own authors recognize this each time and file a follow-up (features_open/012) rather than closing it. That is a reasonable staging choice given the prior guardian veto on breadth, but the council should track whether these follow-ups actually land, since each deferred one is a place real content can still vanish silently on a plan/rebuild path. Otherwise this plan is unusually well-instrumented against the known pattern (durable FACT_CARRY_UNMATCHED_SECTION / FACT_ASSIGNMENT_ABSENT / PLAN_PAGE_MERGE_LOSSY rows, mutation-tested detections, an explicit landmine filed for the sameSectionList %v-comparison bug) and reuses the proven fix shape from cases 4/5 (durable error-channel rows instead of silent drops).

objections.problem: New recordFactAssignmentAbsent (edit 3), recordRecomposeOutcomes (edit 4), and recordLossyPageMerges (edit 5) are three separate hand-written 'loop over misses, write one row per miss to agent_error_log' functions written in the same PR. The landmine index already names a family built for exactly this — LogActionFindings / LogActionEntryFindings alongside LogActionEntry / LogActionError in platform/orchestration/actions/log_action_error.go — and nothing in the rationale or grounded_in shows these three new functions were checked against that existing multi-finding logger before three bespoke ones were written. If LogActionFindings already does 'persist N distinct finding rows with a code/detail per row', these three should call it, not duplicate its loop-and-insert shape three times in one round.

RECOMPOSE_INTENT_NOT_REALISED and PLAN_PAGE_MERGE_LOSSY are brand-new error_code values introduced without a query in grounded_in confirming no code already reports 'planner ignored realised composition' or 'page merge dropped content' under a different existing code (e.g. an existing snapped_sections/reconcile diagnostic path). Given agent_error_log already carries FACT_CARRY_UNMATCHED_SECTION and FACT_SCOPING_EMPTY_COMPOSITION for adjacent situations in this same file, a check that no sibling code already covers this case is warranted before adding two more codes.

missing: No check shown against LogActionFindings/LogActionEntryFindings before writing three new record*Outcomes/record*Absent/record*LossyMerges functions.
reviews.notes: This is a mature resubmission with strong reuse discipline overall: it extends existing functions (carrySectionFactsOntoRealised, sameSectionList, dedupePlanPageRows) rather than forking new ones, reuses the agent_error_log channel established by earlier rounds, and reuses existing seeds/agents. The one gap is the three new 'record a batch of misses as rows' functions added in this round without visible evidence they were checked against the existing LogActionFindings/LogActionEntryFindings family the landmine index says already exists for this exact shape. Not architecture-severity — flagging as object so the author closes the gap with one grep, not to block the substantive change.

No load-bearing rule (WRAPPER-ORCHESTRATOR, WORK-ITEM DEDUP, TRUTHFUL PROVENANCE, DECLARED CONTRACTS, SCHEMA-SOURCE TIERS, or COLUMN RENAME/DROP) is violated by this plan: all edits are either Go code shipped through the normal build/deploy path or jsonb_set config seeds with DO/RAISE ordering guards, no DDL, no work-item creation, no new orchestration steps run inline. On DECLARED CONTRACTS: facts_scoped/assigned_fact_ids/assigned_writer_block are new sub-fields nested inside the already-passed section_plan input (input_mapping 'section_plan':'section_plan' pre-exists per the plan's own SERVING-PATH evidence), and per the platform's documented output_contract behaviour (naming output_field NAMES only, not nested field shapes) the input/output contract mechanism appears to operate at the same top-level granularity -- so this is consistent with existing (if awkward) platform convention, not a new violation. This is itself a guideline-gap worth flagging for amendment: the contract rule's exemption clause is silent on whether nested-field additions to an already-declared object input need re-declaration, and that ambiguity should be resolved by a ruling rather than left to plan-by-plan judgement. The plan's own correction of a prior editquality HIGH miss (point 1) and its explicit call-out of the sameSectionList prompt-redefines-metric landmine (edit 2) show good landmine discipline; the one thing worth a second look before merge is the census methodology in the check above.

Registry/handler resolution is by seed path against agent_definitions default_config, not filename convention; edit 7's sketch explicitly quotes the full nested jsonb path (workflow->steps->process_sections_loop->config->sub_workflow->steps->generate_content->config->prompt_template) rather than assuming a flat key, which is exactly the discipline this seat checks for. No new ad-hoc bundling/context-gathering code is added — the plan modifies existing Go actions (v3_site_actions.go, write_site_plan_action.go) and existing seed-config mechanisms (docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/*.sql), which is the platform's own configuration channel. The round shows travelling-docs discipline itself (doc_notes/owner rulings referenced, DECISIONS_*.md, COMPLIANCE_READ_*.md) rather than reinventing it. No doc-hygiene tooling (dedup/thin_versions/archiving) is touched or reimplemented. Ordering guards use DO/RAISE against agent_definitions state directly rather than a hand-rolled parallel check. No landmine-relevant filename-based handler resolution or duplicate-active-row hazard applies (the round itself measured 1/1/1 active rows). Approve.

objections.problem: reconcilePlanWithRealised / carrySectionFactsOntoRealised is shared plumbing behind THREE agent workflows (build-site-planner, page-build-handler, page-content-writer per the plan's own census). This round again touches all three via config_change seeds plus the shared Go path in one submission — the exact breadth shape a prior guardian veto (round 1, corr 902a8563) flagged. The plan argues this is the 'sliced consumption half' that veto asked for, but three agent_definitions rows are still being wired together with ordering-dependent DO/RAISE guards. Containable, but the council should confirm the prior veto's breadth concern is actually satisfied and not just re-labelled.

sameSectionList's %v-comparison bug silently changed what snapped_sections counts (a landmine the plan itself names). The plan asserts 'nothing in this lane's docs quotes such a figure' but that is self-assessed, not measured against consumers outside this lane (e.g. dashboards, other reports reading agent_error_log/orchestration logs for that counter).

missing: Whether any consumer outside platform/orchestration/actions reads snapped_sections/snapped_rename/unioned_in as a metric — the plan's claim that none do is asserted, not measured against a fleet-wide grep, and code_checks cannot see string-literal usage reliably.
reviews.notes: No core-plumbing (coordinator/kafka/spawn/dispatch) touched, so stability-preference deflection check not triggered. Workflow-JSON edits (328/330/362) are correctly operation config_change and each names its owning pipeline/agent, satisfying surface-ownership. Blast radius is confined to platform/orchestration/actions (two files) plus three agent_definitions rows in one functional chain (plan->build->write), not architecture-change scale (not shared wire formats across services, not exported cross-package signatures). The 176-line-window containment claim for object-form leakage is backed by an end-to-end test per the plan, which is the right control. Recommend REVISE-not-VETO: the breadth objection is precedent-relevant (see checks) and should be confirmed resolved rather than re-litigated blind.

This plan touches site-planner/page-build-handler/page-content-writer workflow config, plan reconciliation, and observability rows (FACT_CARRY_UNMATCHED_SECTION, FACT_ASSIGNMENT_ABSENT, RECOMPOSE_INTENT_NOT_REALISED, PLAN_PAGE_MERGE_LOSSY) — none of it is the diagnosis loop (090/097 diagnose-* agents, diagnosis_artifacts, sqlguard/read-only SQL layers, doc_notes note-filing, error_step config, or pod/token isolation). New records are explicitly all LogActionError/agent_error_log warnings that do not gate or fail any plan/save (edits 3-5 note tests pin the no-op cases), consistent with observability-never-costs-a-run outside this loop's own discipline anyway. No error_step routing added. No SQL guard layers touched. No token/pod placement changes. Out of scope for this council seat; approve.

This round is internal plumbing (fact-assignment carry/wiring) plus a writer-prompt change (seed 330 v4) that narrows what facts a section may cite, moving TOWARD smallest-true-claim discipline rather than away from it: scoped sections get only their assigned facts, factless sections get an explicit no-facts instruction, and the unscoped fallback is asserted byte-identical to today. The cited compliance read (COMPLIANCE_READ_2026-08-10_writer_prompt_v4.md) reports no infallibility/overclaimed-reliability phrasing and no poisoned-spec instruction in the operative text — I cannot see that plaintext directly in this submission, only its hash and the author's summary, so this approval leans on that prior review having been done honestly; if it resurfaces without that artefact attached, re-check it. New error-channel rows (FACT_ASSIGNMENT_ABSENT, RECOMPOSE_INTENT_NOT_REALISED, PLAN_PAGE_MERGE_LOSSY) are observability additions only, do not touch banned_claims/evidence gates, and do not alter any shipped plan by themselves (tests pin the no-op cases). No disclaimers, legal pages, real-named-entity copy, or tool-result surfaces are touched. Residual note for other seats: seed 362's redesign-escape is prose-only, so a released page can silently keep verbatim old content or drop — that's a completeness/accuracy risk worth someone tracking, not itself a fabricated-claim or legal-surface issue.

objections.problem: RECOMPOSE_INTENT_NOT_REALISED's absent_from_plan branch cannot distinguish a genuine drop from a rename (author-stated limitation) — matches the general 016 pattern of a detection that measures a symptom class rather than the cause; acceptable as observability-only but should not be read as a defect-rate count.

The 328/330 DO/RAISE ordering guards use IS NULL / LIKE-on-prose checks rather than the jsonb <> / = comparisons the landmine index warns rot silently — correctly avoided here, but confirm both guards were actually executed standalone against live (unapplied) state as claimed, not just reasoned about, since a guard that never fires is the exact 016 trap.

reviews.notes: This submission is unusually disciplined for config/jsonb surgery: dry-run+forced-rollback tested against live rows, verify blocks proven able to fail by induced mutation, ordering guards induced standalone against live state, mutation-tested Go changes with the build-failure-vs-test-failure distinction explicitly caught and corrected (matches 016's mutant/build-failure lore directly), and post-roll pod-verification re-run against the NEW pod names after a roll changed them (matches the 'fleet is mixed after a roll' and 'verify against the pod not git' lore). The four active-row hazard and the loop-nested-prompt census hazard (both documented landmines) were explicitly measured and addressed. The counter-redefinition bug (sameSectionList's %v compare) is itself filed as a landmine by the author, which is the right instinct. No git/tag-only deploy verification, no naive replace()-style SQL, no repair-vs-regenerate applicability. Residual risks are self-disclosed with correct severity.

Root-cause fixes throughout: name-based section matching replaces the positional cross-reference RFC_016 flags as the actual defect; sameSectionList's %v-comparison bug is corrected at its source, not patched around; seed 362 gives the planner the missing visibility (realised sections) rather than papering over drift downstream. Deferrals are explicit and justified: imagery scope_ref (bugs_open/214) and the permanent recompose_pages field-based fix (features_open/012) are named, reasoned, and routed to follow-ups rather than silently skipped. Reuse is demonstrated, not asserted — composeWriterBlock, sectionEntryName, and the existing agent_error_log channel are extended rather than duplicated; struct-return signature changes are stated as deliberate extensions, satisfying no-silent-rename. Config edits target the fully nested workflow path (process_sections_loop.sub_workflow.steps.generate_content), correctly navigating the loop-nested-prompt landmine rather than falling into the top-level-only census trap. Observability additions (FACT_ASSIGNMENT_ABSENT, RECOMPOSE_INTENT_NOT_REALISED, PLAN_PAGE_MERGE_LOSSY) are framed and tested as detection of disobedience/loss, not as masking of a known defect, and the plan says so plainly. No interpolated SQL; jsonb_set/DO-RAISE patterns are consistent with the platform's seed-file conventions. Tone is plain and evidence-led throughout.

This is a pipeline-mechanics fix: it repairs fact-assignment carry-through from planner to writer, fixes a broken change-detection counter, and adds durable observability (miss records) rather than silent overrides. Downstream behaviour on failure/disobedience explicitly falls back to today's byte-identical unscoped behaviour (facts_scoped absent -> unscoped arm), which is the correct 'mark and surface, don't silently substitute' pattern the mission calls for. No revenue-shape or site-type decision is touched; classifier direction and its outputs are not shortcut or bypassed anywhere in this diff. Ordering guards (DO/RAISE) prevent partial application rather than silently degrading. Mission-neutral, restores intended behaviour of an existing content-fidelity mechanism.

objections.problem: Rationale (5) reverses a prior council-upheld claim ('exactly one live agent wires spec_sections') to a new claim ('TWO agents run plan_sections, NEITHER wires spec_sections; page-build-handler is the serving path via call_content_writer input_mapping'). This determines which agent seed 328 correctly targets. The census SQL and input_mapping content are asserted with timestamps but not independently checked here — attaching verification.

The '1/1/1 active non-snapshot row' measurement (rationale 2) is load-bearing for both seed 328 and 330 actually reaching the loaded row — landmine 'Four agent types have TWO active definition rows, and only the higher version is ever loaded' documents this exact failure mode elsewhere in the fleet. Plausible but unverified from this seat.

missing: Whether corr a06ff850 (the original submission this resubmits) or bugs_open/087, bugs_open/215, bugs_open/214, RFC_016, or seeds 328/330/333/362 have prior council_report history with objections not addressed here.
reviews.notes: This resubmission is unusually evidence-dense (pod-greps, mutation tests, census SQL, hashes) and explicitly engages several landmines already on file (counter-redefinition-by-prompt-edit, chassis log retention, duplicate active agent rows), which is the correct posture. No new mechanism appears to duplicate an already-named existing one — edits 3-5 are incremental extensions of an already-shipped edit 1/2, and edit 4/5's new detections are explicitly scoped as interim per owner ruling with a named permanent-fix ticket (features_open/012). My remaining concern is narrow: the single reversal of a previously-upheld absence/wiring claim (rationale 5) is the crux of seed 328's correctness and deserves independent confirmation before the round treats it as settled, since every downstream reviewer inherits it. Approving with checks attached rather than objecting outright, since the claims are specific and falsifiable rather than bare assertions.

missing: Did not verify whether 'plan_sections' step config being read by two different agent types (page-build-handler, page-content-writer) has previously been treated as a de facto shared contract in any past council round — worth a human check if this pattern recurs with a THIRD consumer.
reviews.notes:
ARCHITECTURE_SIGNAL: point_fix | DEFLECTIONS: unknown

Future load being judged: per-section fact scoping so writer prompts stop repeating site-wide evidence blocks. The mechanism used to carry it — an opt-in jsonb key on an existing shared workflow step (plan_sections' section_facts, prompt template branching on facts_scoped) — is the platform's established extension point for agent behaviour, not a new one. That's the right call: no schema column, no new exported symbol consumed by other packages, no coordinated edit across 3+ top-level packages (everything Go-side sits in platform/orchestration/actions, and the two touched functions are private). The trigger test in (c) does not fire.

The one place I looked hardest for a smuggled shared mechanism was the object-form entries the carry writes into pages['sections'] between reconcile (:3101) and normalise (:3277) in v3_site_actions.go — that's the core cache format 15+ readers depend on, per the landmine index. But the plan itself names this as the thing to watch, bounds it to a 176-line window inside one function, and pins it with an end-to-end test rather than a comment. That is the correct scope discipline for a contained fix touching a sensitive shared structure — it is not introducing a new contract, it is temporarily borrowing an existing one under test.

Cost of not changing: if this stayed unshipped, the counter-meaning bug (sameSectionList's %v comparison silently redefined by a prompt edit) keeps miscounting composition changes as changes, and disobedient/absent fact assignments stay invisible — both real but bounded defects, not blocked capabilities. Apply-order DO/RAISE guards are config safety, not a staged-rollout architecture signal.

No objections at architecture level; this is design continuation of an already owner-ruled direction (RFC_016), sliced per the prior guardian breadth veto.
